name: Kansas
overview: Kansas offers three mutually exclusive homeowner refund routes, with different income definitions.

programs.name: Homestead Refund (K-40H)
programs.ageRule: Born before January1,1970; or qualifying disability/blindness; or qualifying dependent child.
programs.incomeDefinition: Household income, including 50% of Social Security under K-40H rules.
programs.formulaSummary: Income-table percentage of qualifying property taxes, subject to program cap.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Kansas residence, owner occupancy, and $350,000 home-value limit.
interactions: Only one of K-40H, K-40PT and K-40SVR per household.
programs.programYear: 2025 property taxes/income; claim normally due April15,2026.

programs.name: SAFESR (K-40PT)
programs.incomeDefinition: SAFESR household-income definition; not the newer K-40SVR KAGI definition.
programs.maximumBenefit: 75% of qualifying taxes actually and timely paid.
programs.formulaSummary: Refunds 75% of eligible homestead property taxes.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year residence, owner occupancy, and $350,000 home-value limit.
interactions: Mutually exclusive with K-40H and K-40SVR.

programs.name: Seniors and Disabled Veterans Refund (K-40SVR)
programs.ageRule: Qualifying senior age65+, disabled veteran, or eligible surviving spouse.
programs.incomeDefinition: From 2025: total Kansas adjusted gross income of all household members.
programs.maximumBenefit: Qualifying tax increase over the program base year.
programs.formulaSummary: Current eligible homestead tax minus eligible base-year tax.
eligibilityNotes: Full-year Kansas residence and owner occupancy.
interactions: Mutually exclusive with K-40H and K-40PT.
programs.programYear: 2025 current-year taxes/income and applicable historical base year.

researchNotes: Renters are not eligible for these three programs.
K-40SVR changed household income in 2025; K-40H and SAFESR definitions did not change.
Claims can be advanced to pay property taxes, so cash timing can precede filing.
